Tuesday 3 November 2026 · written 05:12 SGT

Oil plunges 8% on Iran draft as defensives lead, tech slides

  • US equities split as S&P 500 fell 0.50% and Nasdaq fell 1.08% while Dow rose 0.41% on an 8% oil slide that pulled 10-year yields lower.
  • Technology fell 2.97% and semis fell 2.76% on AI-spending fears and a cautious Kioxia guide, while staples rose 1.58% and financials rose 1.84% on defensive rotation.
  • WTI fell 7.90% to $95.89 and Brent fell 8.31% to $104 on a reported draft Iran peace, lifting airlines with United up 4.80%, while gold rose 1.40% from one-year lows.
  • Crypto stayed soft as Bitcoin fell 1.45% on $643 million in ETF outflows and Binance saw $4.6 billion in withdrawals, with BNB down 1.83% and Solana down 2.95%.

What happened

Macro and rates: oil drop pulls yields lower

Treasury yields eased with the US 10-year down 2.9 basis points to 4.90% as WTI fell 7.90% to $95.89 and Brent fell 8.31% to $104 on reports a draft Iran peace was circulating. The move lifted futures slightly after a volatile week and steadied the dollar index down 0.12%, while VIX stayed elevated at 21.54.

Yields falling with oil matches prior episodes where energy-led inflation fears receded, supporting a defensive tilt. Asia was mixed and Europe closed higher on cheaper oil, underscoring the macro driver over single-stock news.

Sources WSJ, upi, Crude Oil Prices Today, The Guardian, Bloomberg.com, bloomingbit, CNBC, Finimize

US equities: tech lags, defensives and airlines lead

US stocks split with S&P 500 down 0.50% to 7,542.15 and Nasdaq down 1.08% while the Dow rose 0.41%, led by sector rotation. Technology fell 2.97% and semis 2.76% on AI capex bubble worries and a cautious Kioxia outlook that hit Micron down 5.85% and Western Digital down 7.52%, while Oracle fell 8.76% on a $20 billion stock and bond raise.

Defensives outperformed with staples up 1.58%, utilities up 0.58%, financials up 1.84%, industrials up 1.40% and materials up 1.73%, the biggest tech-to-staples shift since 2001. Airlines jumped as fuel fell, with United up 4.80% and Delta up 4.08%, confirming a scope-matched cause.

Sources 24/7 Wall St., Yahoo Finance, Stock Titan, Benzinga, Investing.com, marketscreener.com, Barron's, Quartz, Bloomberg.com, Reuters

Commodities: crude tumbles, metals bounce

Crude slid below $100 on diplomacy hopes, with headlines tying the drop to easing supply fears after attacks on Iran's South Pars field earlier. Natural gas fell 1.07% to $2.87 and touched 11-week lows on record output and warm US temperatures, while European gas prices also eased on LNG relief hopes.

Gold rose 1.40% to $3,953.60 and silver rose 2.70% to $50.60 rebounding from one-year lows after an 11% plunge, aided by softer oil and a midterms watch. Copper held up 0.96% despite tech weakness as Chile outlook supported prices.

Sources WSJ, Crude Oil Prices Today, Fortune, EnergyNow.com, Natural Gas Intelligence, BullionVault, Kitco, StoneX, The Northern Miner

Crypto: ETF outflows and hack fallout weigh

Bitcoin fell 1.45% to $76,774 and ether eased 0.65% as spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $643 million in outflows led by BlackRock and Fidelity, the largest in four months after the record Binance hack. Binance clients withdrew more than $4.6 billion and BNB fell 1.83% even as some withdrawals resumed, while Solana fell 2.95% on a $95.9 million hacker swap and whale sales.

Relative strength was narrow with TRON up 1.76% as USDT supply on TRON overtook Ethereum, averaging $90.75 billion, and XRP held near $1.25 on adoption and ETF inflow talk. Bitcoin's resilience masked jitters as trust issues lingered.

Sources Yahoo Finance, CoinDesk, CryptoTicker.io, CBS News, Bloomberg.com, AMBCrypto, CoinMarketCap, Crypto News, Santiment, Benzinga
